claim: Stu2p/XMAP215 proteins are essential microtubule polymerases that use multiple αβ-tubulin-interacting TOG domains to bind microtubule plus ends and catalyze fast microtubule growth.
source: Stu2p/XMAP215 proteins are essential microtubule polymerases that use multiple αβ-tubulin-interacting TOG domains to bind microtubule plus ends and catalyze fast microtubule growth.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the abstract that draws from established knowledge about these proteins and is supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: TOG2 binds selectively to a fully 'curved' conformation of αβ-tubulin, incompatible with a microtubule lattice.
source: Like TOG1, TOG2 binds selectively to a fully 'curved' conformation of αβ-tubulin, incompatible with a microtubule lattice.
evidence: This claim is supported by the crystal structure determination of TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex presented in the manuscript.

claim: TOG1-TOG2 binds non-cooperatively to two αβ-tubulins.
source: We also show that TOG1-TOG2 binds non-cooperatively to two αβ-tubulins.
evidence: This is supported by analytical ultracentrifugation experiments described in the manuscript.

claim: Preferential interactions between TOGs and fully curved αβ-tubulin that cannot exist elsewhere in the microtubule explain how these polymerases localize to the extreme microtubule end.
source: Preferential interactions between TOGs and fully curved αβ-tubulin that cannot exist elsewhere in the microtubule explain how these polymerases localize to the extreme microtubule end.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The polymerase action changes the configuration of the microtubule end.
source: This tethering model can explain catalyst-like behavior and also predicts that the polymerase action changes the configuration of the microtubule end.
evidence: This is a prediction from the computational model presented in the manuscript.

claim: Microtubules are dynamic polymers of αβ-tubulin that have critical roles in chromosome segregation and intracellular organization.
source: Microtubules are dynamic polymers of αβ-tubulin that have critical roles in chromosome segregation and intracellular organization (reviewed in Desai and Mitchison, 1997).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Evolutionarily conserved proteins in the Stu2p/XMAP215 family regulate microtubule dynamics by promoting fast microtubule elongation.
source: Evolutionarily conserved proteins in the Stu2p/XMAP215 family (Gard and Kirschner, 1987; Ohkura et al., 1988; Wang and Huffaker, 1997) regulate microtubule dynamics by promoting fast microtubule elongation.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: XMAP215 affects the rate of microtubule elongation without affecting the apparent equilibrium.
source: A significant advance in understanding occurred with a landmark study of XMAP215 in which in vitro reconstitution assays demonstrated that the polymerase affected the rate of microtubule elongation without affecting the apparent equilibrium (Brouhard et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Brouhard et al., 2008.

claim: XMAP215 can be described as a catalyst for microtubule elongation.
source: This and other observations (e.g., Shirasu-Hiza et al., 2003; van Breugel et al., 2003) formed the basis for describing XMAP215 as a catalyst for microtubule elongation.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: TOG1 domain from Stu2p binds preferentially to a 'curved' conformation of αβ-tubulin that cannot be incorporated into the body of the microtubule.
source: A recent study from our group revealed that the TOG1 domain from Stu2p binds preferentially to a 'curved' conformation of αβ-tubulin that cannot be incorporated into the body of the microtubule (Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the same group.

claim: A TOG1-TOG2 construct can bind two αβ-tubulins.
source: Our study also showed that a TOG1-TOG2 construct could bind two αβ-tubulins (Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the same group.

claim: The crystal structure of TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex was determined by molecular replacement from crystals that diffracted anisotropically to a minimum Bragg spacing of 2.8 Å.
source: The structure was determined by molecular replacement from crystals that diffracted anisotropically to a minimum Bragg spacing of 2.8 Å (Table 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of experimental data from the crystallography experiments.

claim: The final model of TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex has good geometry with a Molprobity clash score of 1.79 and 95.6% favored residues in Ramachandran plot.
source: The final model has good geometry (Table 1; Molprobity [Chen et al., 2010] clash score 1.79; 95.6% favored residues in Ramachandran plot) and has been refined to an Rfree of 0.259 (Rwork = 0.217).
evidence: This is a direct report of crystallographic refinement statistics.

claim: Conserved residues W341 and R519 on the tubulin-binding surface of TOG2 make very similar contacts with αβ-tubulin as their equivalents in TOG1 (W23 and R200, respectively).
source: Conserved residues like W341 and R519 on the tubulin-binding surface of TOG2 make very similar contacts with αβ-tubulin as their equivalents in TOG1 (W23 and R200, respectively) (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by structural data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The structure of TOG2 bound to αβ-tubulin superimposes with the structure of 'free' TOG2 with 0.7 Å rmsd over 237 Cα atoms.
source: The structure of TOG2 bound to αβ-tubulin superimposes with the structure of 'free' TOG2 (Slep and Vale, 2007) with 0.7 Å rmsd over 237 Cα atoms (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of structural data.

claim: TOG domains are rigid modules that do not change conformation when they bind αβ-tubulin.
source: Because the TOG2 domains pack differently in the 'bound' and 'free' crystals, the similarity in structure suggests that these TOG domains are rigid modules that do not change conformation when they bind αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural comparison data.

claim: The conformation of αβ-tubulin in complex with TOG2 is nearly identical to that seen for TOG1-bound αβ-tubulin (12.3° of curvature in the TOG2 complex vs 13.1° in the TOG1 complex).
source: Even though the structure reported here was obtained from a new crystal form, the conformation of αβ-tubulin in complex with TOG2 is nearly identical to that seen for TOG1-bound αβ-tubulin (Figure 1D) (12.3° of curvature in the TOG2 complex vs 13.1° in the TOG1 complex), and is characteristically distinct from the straight conformation of αβ-tubulin (1° of curvature by our measure) (Löwe et al., 2001; Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of structural data.

claim: Individual tubulin chains between the TOG1 and TOG2 complexes superimpose on each other with 0.4 Å rmsd over Cα atoms.
source: Underscoring this similarity, individual tubulin chains between the TOG1 and TOG2 complexes superimpose on each other with 0.4 Å rmsd over Cα atoms.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison of structural data.

claim: Both TOG1 and TOG2 bind preferentially to the same, curved conformation of αβ-tubulin.
source: Thus, both TOG1 and TOG2 bind preferentially to the same, curved conformation of αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural data presented.

claim: Other TOGs in this family probably also bind to curved αβ-tubulin.
source: By extension, other TOGs in this family probably also bind to curved αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the similarity observed between TOG1 and TOG2.

claim: TOG:αβ-tubulin interactions are required for plus-end localization of Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases.
source: Because TOG:αβ-tubulin interactions are required for plus-end localization of Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases (Al-Bassam et al., 2006), preferential binding of TOGs to curved αβ-tubulin suggests that curved αβ-tubulin itself is the distinctive end-specific feature the polymerase recognizes.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Curved αβ-tubulin itself is the distinctive end-specific feature the polymerase recognizes.
source: Because TOG:αβ-tubulin interactions are required for plus-end localization of Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases (Al-Bassam et al., 2006), preferential binding of TOGs to curved αβ-tubulin suggests that curved αβ-tubulin itself is the distinctive end-specific feature the polymerase recognizes.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the structural data and prior knowledge.

claim: Other plus-end tracking proteins like Eb1 recognize lattice-specific features and consequently show 'comet-like' localization that extends into the microtubule body.
source: In contrast, other plus-end tracking proteins like Eb1 recognize lattice-specific features and consequently show 'comet-like' localization that extends into the microtubule body (Nakamura et al., 2012; Maurer et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: At αβ-tubulin concentrations ranging from 0.08 to 1 μM there is a single dominant peak at 5.8 S with only 1.7 and 2.8% of the material sedimenting faster at the lowest and highest concentration tested.
source: Indeed, at αβ-tubulin concentrations ranging from 0.08 to 1 μM there is a single dominant peak at 5.8 S with only 1.7 and 2.8% of the material sedimenting faster at the lowest and highest concentration tested.
evidence: This is a direct report of analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: TOG1 binds αβ-tubulin with KD = 70 nM.
source: The fits indicate that both TOG domains form relatively tight, 1:1 complexes with αβ-tubulin: TOG1 binds with KD = 70 nM and TOG2 binds with KD = 160 nM.
evidence: This is a direct report of binding affinity measurements from analytical ultracentrifugation experiments.

claim: TOG2 binds αβ-tubulin with KD = 160 nM.
source: The fits indicate that both TOG domains form relatively tight, 1:1 complexes with αβ-tubulin: TOG1 binds with KD = 70 nM and TOG2 binds with KD = 160 nM.
evidence: This is a direct report of binding affinity measurements from analytical ultracentrifugation experiments.

claim: Both TOG domains form relatively tight, 1:1 complexes with αβ-tubulin.
source: The fits indicate that both TOG domains form relatively tight, 1:1 complexes with αβ-tubulin: TOG1 binds with KD = 70 nM and TOG2 binds with KD = 160 nM.
evidence: This is a direct report of binding stoichiometry from analytical ultracentrifugation experiments.

claim: The KD for the TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex is consistent with prior measurement using fluorescence anisotropy and polymerization blocked αβ-tubulin.
source: The KD for the TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex reported here is consistent with our prior measurement using fluorescence anisotropy and polymerization blocked αβ-tubulin (Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior data from the same group.

claim: TOG1 and TOG2 domains are remarkably similar to each other from both a biochemical and a structural perspective.
source: Thus, in addition to a shared preference for the same curved conformation of αβ-tubulin, TOG1 and TOG2 also bind αβ-tubulin with comparable affinities. From both a biochemical and a structural perspective, the TOG1 and TOG2 domains are remarkably similar to each other.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data presented.

claim: TOG1-TOG2 bound to a single αβ-tubulin sediments at 7.1 S.
source: First, using mutations on TOG1-TOG2 that disrupt the slightly weaker TOG2:αβ-tubulin interactions, we determined that TOG1-TOG2 bound to a single αβ-tubulin sediments at 7.1 S (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct report of analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: Using a mixture in which αβ-tubulin was superstoichiometric with respect to TOG1-TOG2, a larger species sedimenting at 9.1 S was observed.
source: Next, using a mixture in which αβ-tubulin was superstoichiometric with respect to TOG1-TOG2 (Figure 3C), we observed a larger species sedimenting at 9.1 S.
evidence: This is a direct report of analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: The data are not consistent with models that assume even modest 10-fold positive or negative cooperativity.
source: The resulting signal weighted average sedimentation coefficients are not consistent with models that assume even modest 10-fold positive or negative cooperativity (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an analysis of the analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: The data are much better described by a model in which each TOG domain in TOG1-TOG2 interacts independently with its αβ-tubulin.
source: Instead, the data are much better described by a model in which each TOG domain in TOG1-TOG2 interacts independently with its αβ-tubulin (the best fit was obtained from a model invoking less than twofold negative cooperativity, not shown).
evidence: This is an analysis of the analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: Noncooperative binding indicates that αβ-tubulin:αβ-tubulin contacts do not provide additional stability to the TOG1-TOG2:(αβ-tubulin)2 complex.
source: Noncooperative binding contradicts our initial expectation and indicates that αβ-tubulin:αβ-tubulin contacts do not provide additional stability to the TOG1-TOG2:(αβ-tubulin)2 complex.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: The two TOG1-TOG2-bound αβ-tubulins are minimally at an effective concentration of roughly 200 μM.
source: Indeed, allowing 55 Å for the length of each TOG domain and assuming that the ∼75 amino acid linker is flexible and can maximally span 220 Å we estimate that the two TOG1-TOG2-bound αβ-tubulins are minimally at an effective concentration of roughly 200 μM, likely higher because the linker will rarely be fully extended.
evidence: This is a calculation based on structural dimensions.

claim: Observing non-cooperative binding suggests that some property of the TOG1-TOG2 linker antagonizes or counterbalances longitudinal interactions between αβ-tubulins.
source: Observing non-cooperative binding therefore suggests that some property of the TOG1-TOG2 linker antagonizes or counterbalances longitudinal interactions between αβ-tubulins (see below for experiments concerning the linker sequence).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: A construct (TOG2-TOG2) in which TOG1 was replaced by a second copy of TOG2 rescued as well as did the wild-type (TOG1-TOG2).
source: A construct (TOG2-TOG2) in which TOG1 was replaced by a second copy of TOG2 rescued as well as did the wild-type (TOG1-TOG2) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Constructs in which either TOG was impaired for αβ-tubulin binding (TOG1(R200A)-TOG2 or TOG1-TOG2(R519A)) gave full rescue.
source: Constructs in which either TOG was impaired for αβ-tubulin binding (TOG1(R200A)-TOG2 or TOG1-TOG2(R519A)) also gave full rescue (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Under normal conditions, the polymerase can function with only TOG1 or only TOG2 domains.
source: These data indicate that under normal conditions, the polymerase can function with only TOG1 or only TOG2 domains.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Having different TOG domains does not appear to be essential for polymerase function.
source: Thus, having different TOG domains does not appear to be essential for polymerase function.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Stu2p(TOG2-TOG2)-Δcc showed rescue efficiency very similar to that of Stu2p(TOG1-TOG2)-Δcc.
source: Stu2p(TOG2-TOG2)-Δcc showed rescue efficiency very similar to that of Stu2p(TOG1-TOG2)-Δcc (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Dimerization impaired variants of Stu2p in which TOG1 or TOG2 was defective for αβ-tubulin binding did not show any rescue activity.
source: Dimerization impaired variants of Stu2p in which TOG1 or TOG2 was defective for αβ-tubulin binding did not show any rescue activity (Figure 4B), consistent with a prior in vitro study of XMAP215 that demonstrated a requirement for at least two TOG domains (Widlund et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: XMAP215 requires at least two TOG domains.
source: Dimerization impaired variants of Stu2p in which TOG1 or TOG2 was defective for αβ-tubulin binding did not show any rescue activity (Figure 4B), consistent with a prior in vitro study of XMAP215 that demonstrated a requirement for at least two TOG domains (Widlund et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Both shuffled linkers gave rescue activity nearly indistinguishable from the wild-type linker.
source: Both shuffled linkers gave rescue activity nearly indistinguishable from the wild-type linker (Figure 5A), consistent with the robust rescue activity of alternatively linked functional TOGs in dimeric Stu2p(TOG1-TOG2(R519A)) and Stu2p(TOG1(R200A)-TOG2) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: The sequence linking the two functional TOG domains tolerates significant variation.
source: Thus, the sequence linking the two functional TOG domains tolerates significant variation.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic rescue assay data with shuffled linkers.

claim: Deleting 14 amino acids from the TOG1-TOG2 linker had little effect on rescue activity.
source: Deleting 14 amino acids had little effect on rescue activity (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Rescue activity was mildly compromised by deletions of 22, 32, 40, and 50 amino acids from the TOG1-TOG2 linker.
source: Rescue activity was mildly compromised by deletions of 22, 32, 40, and 50 amino acids (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Deleting 60 amino acids from the TOG1-TOG2 linker substantially abolished rescue activity.
source: Deleting 60 amino acids from the TOG1-TOG2 linker substantially abolished rescue activity (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a direct report of genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Stu2p function is compromised when the sequence linking two TOG domains becomes too short.
source: These data suggest that Stu2p function is compromised when the sequence linking two TOG domains becomes too short.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the genetic rescue assay data with linker deletions.

claim: Linker lengths below ∼40 amino acids occur very rarely in ∼300 Stu2p/XMAP215 orthologs.
source: This analysis showed that linker lengths below ∼40 amino acids occur very rarely (Figure 5C), supporting the notion that there is a minimal linker length below which polymerase function is compromised.
evidence: This is a direct report of evolutionary analysis data.

claim: There is a minimal linker length below which polymerase function is compromised.
source: This analysis showed that linker lengths below ∼40 amino acids occur very rarely (Figure 5C), supporting the notion that there is a minimal linker length below which polymerase function is compromised.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the evolutionary analysis and genetic rescue assay data.

claim: Plus-end localization of the polymerase occurs by a TOG domain binding to curved αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end.
source: The central elements of this model are: (i) plus-end localization of the polymerase occurs by a TOG domain binding to curved αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end;
evidence: This is a component of the proposed tethering model.

claim: Full curvature of αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end requires that it not have any lateral neighbors.
source: (ii) full curvature of αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end requires that it not have any lateral neighbors;
evidence: This is a component of the proposed tethering model based on structural data.

claim: αβ-tubulin bound to the other TOG domain is physically tethered to the microtubule end and therefore associates with it more frequently.
source: (iii) αβ-tubulin bound to the other TOG domain is physically tethered to the microtubule end and therefore associates with it more frequently.
evidence: This is a component of the proposed tethering model.

claim: When not engaged with αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end, the polymerase diffuses on the microtubule lattice by virtue of its basic domain.
source: When not engaged with αβ-tubulin at the microtubule end, we assume based on results from others (Brouhard et al., 2008) that the polymerase diffuses on the microtubule lattice by virtue of its basic domain, thereby rapidly 'searching' for another curved αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is an assumption in the model based on prior work.

claim: XMAP215 has been shown to promote the elongation of microtubules in the presence of a hydrolysis resistant GTP analog.
source: Because XMAP215 has been shown to promote the elongation of microtubules in the presence of a hydrolysis resistant GTP analog (Brouhard et al., 2008), we performed 'GTP-only' simulations (no GTP hydrolysis) to simplify the behavior by eliminating catastrophe.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Enhanced trapping of longitudinally-associated αβ-tubulin through the tethering effect shows catalyst-like activity: growth rates and apparent on-rate constant (slope) both change significantly but the apparent equilibrium for growth (x-intercept) does not.
source: Enhanced trapping of longitudinally-associated αβ-tubulin through the tethering effect shows catalyst-like activity: growth rates and apparent on-rate constant (slope) both change significantly but the apparent equilibrium for growth (x-intercept) does not.
evidence: This is a direct report of simulation results.

claim: Tethering-enhanced associative trapping of weakly-bound singletons can recapitulate the essence of catalyst-like activity.
source: Affecting the rate but not the apparent equilibrium indicates that tethering-enhanced associative trapping of weakly-bound singletons can recapitulate the essence of catalyst-like activity.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the simulation results.

claim: The simple model shows the modest overall stimulation that is characteristic of these polymerases.
source: Thus, in addition to capturing catalyst-like action, our simple model also shows the modest overall stimulation that is characteristic of these polymerases.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the simulation results.

claim: The low population and lifetime of longitudinally associated αβ-tubulin substrate was limiting the activity obtainable in the model.
source: We speculated that because longitudinally associated αβ-tubulin is weakly/transiently bound at the microtubule end (∼mM affinity in our fitted parameters and those of comparable models (VanBuren et al., 2002; Gardner et al., 2011); this compares to working concentrations of αβ-tubulin that are typically at most 20 μM), the low population and lifetime of this 'substrate' was limiting the activity obtainable in our model.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the simulation results and prior work.

claim: Stronger longitudinal affinity gave higher maximal polymerase activity in simulations.
source: We observed in simulations that stronger longitudinal affinity gave higher maximal polymerase activity (Figure 7D, right; see also Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct report of simulation results.

claim: The polymerase activity in the model is related to the population/lifetime of longitudinally-associated αβ-tubulin singleton at the microtubule end.
source: These results support the notion that the polymerase activity in our model is related to the population/lifetime of longitudinally-associated αβ-tubulin singleton at the microtubule end.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the simulation results.

claim: At the MT end, longitudinally-bound αβ-tubulins tend to dissociate much faster than the rate at which unpolymerized αβ-tubulins associate at neighboring sites.
source: The idea is that at the MT end, longitudinally-bound αβ-tubulins tend to dissociate much faster than the rate at which unpolymerized αβ-tubulins associate at neighboring sites.
evidence: This is a component of the proposed mechanism based on the model.

claim: Most of the 'singleton'-type associations are unproductive for elongation, and the MT grows primarily by additions into 'corner' sites.
source: Accordingly, most of the 'singleton'-type associations are unproductive for elongation, and the MT grows primarily by additions into 'corner' sites.
evidence: This is a component of the proposed mechanism based on the model.

claim: Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases enhance elongation by selectively concentrating αβ-tubulin near singleton sites, thereby specifically promoting their associative trapping.
source: In the model we propose, Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases enhance elongation by selectively concentrating αβ-tubulin near singleton sites, thereby specifically promoting their associative trapping.
evidence: This is the core of the proposed tethering mechanism.

claim: The 'trapping complex'—two side-by-side αβ-tubulins without additional neighbors to either side–may be the transition state.
source: We propose that the 'trapping complex'—two side-by-side αβ-tubulins without additional neighbors to either side–may be the transition state.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the model.

claim: The polymerase catalyzes formation of the 'side-by-side' state by selectively concentrating (tethering) the reactants that lead to it.
source: In our model the polymerase catalyzes formation of this 'side-by-side' state by selectively concentrating (tethering) the reactants that lead to it.
evidence: This is a component of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Associative trapping of singletons 'roughens' the microtubule end through the creation of additional, longer-lived 'corner' sites.
source: Associative trapping of singletons also 'roughens' the microtubule end through the creation of additional, longer-lived 'corner' sites.
evidence: This is a prediction from the proposed mechanism.

claim: Rougher microtubule ends can transiently capture unpolymerized subunits more efficiently and independently of the polymerase, through 'filling in'.
source: By virtue of having more favorable sites of interaction, these rougher microtubule ends can transiently capture unpolymerized subunits more efficiently and independently of the polymerase, through 'filling in' (a contribution from filling-in was anticipated previously [Brouhard et al., 2008]).
evidence: This is a prediction from the proposed mechanism, with support from prior work.

claim: Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases localize to the plus end by virtue of preferential interactions between TOG domains and curved αβ-tubulin.
source: In summary, we propose that Stu2p/XMAP215 polymerases localize to the plus end by virtue of preferential interactions between TOG domains and curved αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a summary of the proposed mechanism based on the data presented.

claim: The proposal is consistent with the view that curved, GTP-bound αβ-tubulin is an on-pathway polymerization intermediate.
source: Our proposal is consistent with the view that curved, GTP-bound αβ-tubulin is an on-pathway polymerization intermediate (e.g., Buey et al., 2006; Rice et al., 2008; Nawrotek et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: At least two TOG domains are needed because one TOG is required to bind curved αβ-tubulin on the microtubule and another linked TOG is required for tethering an unpolymerized αβ-tubulin.
source: It also explains the need for at least two TOG domains (Widlund et al., 2011) because one TOG is required to bind curved αβ-tubulin on the microtubule and another linked TOG is required for tethering an unpolymerized αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is an inference from the proposed mechanism and prior work.

claim: Side-by-side trapping and the release of TOG domains will be linked because of the polymerization-associated conformational changes that occur in αβ-tubulin.
source: In this model, side-by-side trapping and the release of TOG domains will be linked because of the polymerization-associated conformational changes that occur in αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a prediction from the proposed mechanism.

claim: The model provides a simple molecular explanation for the catalytic-like action of the polymerase.
source: The model provides a simple molecular explanation for the catalytic-like action of the polymerase, recapitulates the modest maximal stimulation, and rationalizes how a polymerase can be built from domains that bind preferentially to a microtubule-incompatible conformation of αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a summary of the explanatory power of the proposed model.

claim: The model recapitulates the modest maximal stimulation characteristic of these polymerases.
source: The model provides a simple molecular explanation for the catalytic-like action of the polymerase, recapitulates the modest maximal stimulation, and rationalizes how a polymerase can be built from domains that bind preferentially to a microtubule-incompatible conformation of αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a summary of the explanatory power of the proposed model.

claim: The model rationalizes how a polymerase can be built from domains that bind preferentially to a microtubule-incompatible conformation of αβ-tubulin.
source: The model provides a simple molecular explanation for the catalytic-like action of the polymerase, recapitulates the modest maximal stimulation, and rationalizes how a polymerase can be built from domains that bind preferentially to a microtubule-incompatible conformation of αβ-tubulin.
evidence: This is a summary of the explanatory power of the proposed model.

claim: TOG1 is dispensable for the plus-end binding of Stu2p.
source: However, TOG1 is dispensable for the plus-end binding of Stu2p (Al-Bassam et al., 2006), and because of apparent differences in the biochemical behavior of TOG1 and TOG2 (Al-Bassam et al., 2006; Ayaz et al., 2012) we speculated that TOG2 might bind to a different, lattice-induced conformation of αβ-tubulin (Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The crystal structure of TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex was obtained from crystals grown from 25% (vol/vol) PEG 3350, 0.25 M (NH4)2SO4, 0.1 M MES pH 6.1.
source: The crystal used for data collection was grown from 25% (vol/vol) PEG 3350, 0.25 M (NH4)2SO4, 0.1 M MES pH 6.1).
evidence: This is a direct report of crystallization conditions.

claim: Crystals of TOG2:αβ-tubulin complex adopt space group C2 with one complex in the asymmetric unit.
source: Crystals adopt space group C2 with one complex in the asymmetric unit.
evidence: This is a direct report of crystallographic data.

claim: The two TOG1-TOG2-bound αβ-tubulins are at an effective concentration in the range of current estimates for the longitudinal KD for αβ-tubulins.
source: This effective concentration of TOG1-TOG2-bound αβ-tubulin is in the range of current estimates for the longitudinal KD for αβ-tubulins (e.g., Gardner et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work.

claim: Linked TOG domains might stabilize lateral interactions between αβ-tubulins, but these lateral interactions are thought to be much weaker (only molar affinity).
source: Our data do not rule out that linked TOG domains might stabilize lateral interactions between αβ-tubulins because these lateral interactions are thought to be much weaker (only molar affinity [Gardner et al., 2011]): even at effective αβ-tubulin concentrations approaching 1 mM a weak interface like this would not be populated and therefore would contribute little additional stability to the TOG1-TOG2:(αβ-tubulin)2 complex.
evidence: This is a speculation based on prior work and the data presented.

claim: The observation that the two linked TOG domains behave as independent αβ-tubulin binding modules places significant constraints on biochemical models for the mechanism of these polymerases.
source: Whatever the underlying mechanism, the unexpected observation that the two linked TOG domains behave as independent αβ-tubulin binding modules places significant constraints on biochemical models for the mechanism of these polymerases.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the analytical ultracentrifugation data.

claim: Stu2/XMAP215 family polymerases contain at least two different TOG domains.
source: Stu2/XMAP215 family polymerases contain at least two different TOG domains.
evidence: This is established knowledge about these proteins.

claim: Ablating the function of individual TOGs shows compromised rescue under conditions of microtubule stress.
source: Ablating the function of individual TOGs is not without functional consequences under more stringent conditions, because these same constructs do show compromised rescue under conditions of microtubule stress (Ayaz et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work from the same group.

claim: Dimerization impaired Stu2p only partially compensated for the depletion of endogenous Stu2p.
